## Data cleaning

Firstly, use a function to automatically remove all the empty or single-value columns to remove irrelevant variables. Secondly, filter the data and only keep the YIELD data.

```{r}
# 1. Load necessary libraries
# We use 'tidyverse' for all data manipulation (dplyr, readr, stringr)
library(tidyverse)

# 2. Define the function to remove single-value columns
# This function checks each column. If a column has only 1 unique value
# (or 0, if it's all NA), it will be removed.
drop_one_value_col <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    dplyr::select(where(~n_distinct(., na.rm = TRUE) > 1))
}

# 3. Load the *original* dataset
cat("Loading 'strawberry_10oct25.csv'...\n")
strawberry <- readr::read_csv("strawberry_10oct25.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) 

# 4. Apply the function to remove single-value columns
cat("Removing columns with only one unique value...\n")
strawberry_skinny <- drop_one_value_col(strawberry)

# 5. Clean and filter the data (REVISED: Type logic removed)
cat("Filtering for all Yield data...\n")
strawberry_yield_cleaned <- strawberry_skinny %>%
  
  # Filter rows to only include 'YIELD' data items
  dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(`Data Item`, "YIELD")) %>%
  
  # Convert 'Value' and 'CV (%)' columns to numeric
  dplyr::mutate(
    Yield_Value = readr::parse_number(Value),
    CV_Percent = readr::parse_number(`CV (%)`)
  ) %>%
  
  # Select and rename the columns we care about
  # (REVISED: 'Type' column is removed)
  dplyr::select(
    Year,
    State,
    Program,
    `Data Item`,
    Yield = Yield_Value,
    CV_Percent
  ) %>%
  
  # Remove any rows where the Yield value is NA
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Yield))

# 6. Save the cleaned data to a new CSV file
output_filename <- "strawberry_yield_cleaned.csv"
readr::write_csv(strawberry_yield_cleaned, output_filename)

cat(paste("\nCleaned data (yield only) saved to:", output_filename, "\n"))
print(head(strawberry_yield_cleaned))
```

## Data Analysis

```{r}
# 2. Load the Cleaned Data
cat("Loading 'strawberry_yield_cleaned.csv'...\n")
df <- read_csv("strawberry_yield_cleaned.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# 3. Filter for "CWT / ACRE"
df_analysis <- df %>%
  filter(str_detect(`Data Item`, "CWT / ACRE"))

cat(paste("Filtered data to", nrow(df_analysis), "rows containing 'CWT / ACRE'.\n"))


# --- 4. New Data Visualizations ---

# Plot 1: Bar Chart of Average Yield by State
plot_avg_yield_bar <- df_analysis %>%
  group_by(State) %>%
  summarise(Mean_Yield = mean(Yield, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(State, Mean_Yield), y = Mean_Yield)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "steelblue") +
    coord_flip() + 
    labs(title = "Average Strawberry Yield by State",
         subtitle = "Filtered for 'YIELD, MEASURED IN CWT / ACRE'",
         x = "State",
         y = "Average Yield (CWT / ACRE)") +
    theme_minimal()

# --- THIS LINE SHOWS THE PLOT ---
print(plot_avg_yield_bar) 
# --------------------------------

# Save the plot
ggsave("avg_yield_by_state_bar.png", plot_avg_yield_bar, width = 8, height = 6)
cat("Saved 'avg_yield_by_state_bar.png'\n")


# Plot 2: Yield vs. Year, Faceted by State
plot_faceted_time <- ggplot(df_analysis, aes(x = Year, y = Yield)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) + 
  facet_wrap(~ State, scales = "free_y") + 
  labs(title = "Strawberry Yield Over Time by State",
       subtitle = "Each state's trend is shown separately",
       x = "Year",
       y = "Yield (CWT / ACRE)") +
  theme_bw() 

# --- THIS LINE SHOWS THE PLOT ---
print(plot_faceted_time)
# --------------------------------

# Save the plot
ggsave("yield_vs_time_faceted.png", plot_faceted_time, width = 10, height = 7)
cat("Saved 'yield_vs_time_faceted.png'\n")

cat("Plots were shown and saved.\n")
```
